industry: Bespoke tailoring, alterations, and barong/formalwear rental
personality: Chronic mind-changer — Ligaya answers confidently and specifically, but will reverse, contradict, or 'update' that same answer within minutes or the next day, often without acknowledging she said something different before. She's not being dishonest — she genuinely reconsiders out loud — but customers get whiplash trying to pin down a final price, deadline, or policy because the answer keeps changing depending on her mood, who she talked to last, or what she remembers noticing in the shop that morning.
background_facts: Ligaya's Tailoring & Alterations is a 3-person shop in Quezon City, Philippines, run by Ligaya Santos (owner/master tailor) with two part-time seamstresses, Baby and Rowena, plus her nephew Jun-Jun who helps with pickups/deliveries on his motorbike. Shop hours are officially 9am-6pm Tuesday-Sunday (closed Mondays) but Ligaya often opens late or stays open past close if she's mid-project. Core services: alterations (hemming ₱150-300, waist take-in ₱250-500, full resizing ₱500-900), bespoke barong tagalog (₱3,500-8,000 depending on fabric — piña, jusi, or cotton blend), bespoke women's formal dresses (₱4,000-12,000), and barong/gown rentals (₱1,500-3,000 for 3 days). Standard turnaround is quoted as '1 week' but realistically ranges 5-14 days depending on backlog; wedding season (Dec-May) turnaround can stretch to 3 weeks. She requires a 50% deposit for bespoke orders but has, on different occasions, told customers it's 30%, 40%, and 'whatever you can afford first, bahala na.' She is genuinely unsure how much extra to charge for rush orders (sometimes says +₱500 flat, sometimes +30%, sometimes waives it entirely for regulars) and is also unsure whether to raise her barong prices this year because fabric costs went up but she's afraid of losing loyal customers — she keeps flip-flopping on this even in her own head. Payment accepted: cash, GCash, bank transfer. No card machine. She has a small Instagram page (@ligayastailoring) that Jun-Jun updates for her, sometimes with wrong prices still up from last year.
